The point being made above is that, legally speaking, marriage is a contract. That contract involves an agreement between multiple parties which can have obligations or responsibilities arising as a part of that contract. The religious aspect of these justifications can be evaluated separately and I'll attempt to do so for clarity although it is necessary to understand these as well as the biological underpinnings to appreciate the structure of the contract in general.

From the strictly legal standpoint, the government's duty is enforcing a contract. This is an inherent in its own social contract with the governed. The purpose of this obligation is prevention of fraud and abuse against its citizens. Even the most anarcho-capitalistic voluntaryist recognizes this function as a valid function even though they will suggest a private market-based alternative. Regardless, when one party chooses to neglect their responsibility under a contract it is rightly considered fraudulent activity. The remedies can involve imprisonment of the offender, enforcement of the duties with compensatory damages or dissolution of the contract. In this case, you're voiding the option to impose enforcement and it's already generally agreed that it's illogical to imprison someone. The logical consequence is that this necessitates either permitting the fraud to continue unabated or to permit dissolution of the contract. (aka divorce)

The purpose of maintaining the enforcement is very simple: preventing fraudulent activity which deprives one party by neglecting the obligations of the other. A wife consistently and intransigently choosing not to have sex with her husband is neglecting the legal responsibility she has to her partner under the social contract. In terms of biology, this serves a very specific purpose. The man's interest is not having his resources taken from him to provide for children that do not carry his genes. We called this obligation "fidelity." The woman's interest is receiving resources and protection from a man. We called this obligation being a "breadwinner." This arrangement forms the underlying biological framework for marriage and the contract is a formalization of the pair bond that this exchange relies upon. Obviously, the biological principle isn't at play in every relationship. But this is the normative justification that establishes the general rule which defines the contract.

You have effectively removed the remedy for fraudulent exchange in the case where a woman chooses not to fulfill the objective of primary interest to the man. This is only one step short of an illegitimate relationship where she actually sleeps around. In a prolonged state such a thing may reasonably be considered fraud. Less overt than the fraud committed by a woman sleeping with the mail man. But fraud nonetheless since the husband is no longer receiving a benefit of the contract because the wife refuses to fulfill her conjugal responsibility to him.

It's also necessary to dive into the religious aspect of this contract to understand the objectives formed by it. The dissolution is clearly held to be a non-preferential outcome as it was permitted only in cases of infidelity. Indeed, divorce without a specific cause of infidelity is considered a sin. The obligations of marriage are explicitly stated to include a conjugal relationship and it is stated that any failure to maintain such a relationship should only operate as a temporary arrangement. Otherwise, it encourages violations of fidelity.

It's fair to admit that when the contract was originally defined it was based more on the arrangement of the parents than the people who are being married. However, this is no longer the case. The contract is generally a voluntary arrangement. Therefore, when you refuse a legal remedy to the contract which requires its enforcement you are necessitating the undesirable conclusion of dissolution or you are engaging in entrapment which causes the man to have to fulfill his responsibilities without the woman fulfilling hers. Issues like this were why the Catholic Church, which was the primary officiator of such relationships in the Middle Ages, provided the option for the annulment of an unconsummated marriage.

The problem now is that so many people don't understand the expectations and intentions of this contract and these have been attenuated by people who choose to seek "marriage" yet violate that contract implicitly. By doing so the entire contract itself has become a "tar baby" for many people which causes them to either avoid it entirely or disdain it. Prudence, therefore, dictates that many men and women simply avoid the entire thing and stay single. If you wanted a relationship where these obligations didn't apply, you should have defined that relationship as something else and not subverted the definition of marriage.
